nodes.text: Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that, for any $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_n\}\subseteq [2,\infty)\cap\mathbb{N}$ of size $n$, in any interval $I$ of $f(n)\max(A)$ consecutive integers there exist distinct $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in I$ such that $a_i\mid x_i$. Obtain good bounds for $f(n)$, or even an asymptotic formula.

#709 : [ErSu59] [Er92c] number theory A problem of Erdős and Surányi [ErSu59] , who proved\[(\log n)^c \ll f(n) \ll n^{1/2}\]for some constant $c>0$. The lower bound here can be improved, using van Doorn's lower bound for [711] from [vD26] , to\[\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\ll f(n).\]See also [708] .
